questions.questionText: The doctor advised him to ___ from oily food for a few weeks.
questions.explanation: 'Abstain from' means to keep away from something; the other verbs do not take 'from' in this sense.

questions.questionText: Heavy rain ___ the match, so it was postponed to Sunday.
questions.explanation: The match was postponed, so the rain interrupted it: 'disrupted' fits.

questions.questionText: Ravi is very ___; he never tells a lie.
questions.explanation: Never telling a lie describes an honest person.

questions.questionText: The old man is so ___ that he donates half his pension to charity.
questions.explanation: Giving away money freely shows generosity; 'stingy' is the opposite.

questions.questionText: The sun was so ___ at noon that we could not walk barefoot on the road.
questions.explanation: Hot road surface needs an intensely hot sun: 'scorching'.

questions.questionText: The teacher praised Anita for her ___ in solving the toughest problem.
questions.explanation: Praise goes with a positive quality; 'ingenuity' means cleverness.

questions.questionText: The thief ___ the policeman by hiding behind a pillar.
questions.explanation: 'Elude' means to escape or avoid someone cleverly.

questions.questionText: He was so ___ after the long trek that he fell asleep immediately.
questions.explanation: Falling asleep at once follows extreme tiredness: 'exhausted'.

questions.questionText: Wearing a seat belt is ___ for the driver, as the law requires it.
questions.explanation: 'As the law requires it' means compulsory: 'mandatory'.

questions.questionText: The judge ___ the accused of all charges due to lack of evidence.
questions.explanation: Lack of evidence leads to being cleared of charges: 'acquitted'.

questions.questionText: The magician's trick left the audience ___; nobody could explain it.
questions.explanation: Being unable to explain something leaves people puzzled: 'baffled'.

questions.questionText: Rahul's ___ for cricket began when he received his first bat at the age of six.
questions.explanation: A gift that starts an interest in cricket creates a passion, not an aversion.

questions.questionText: The ___ of the old fort is a major tourist attraction in Rajasthan.
questions.explanation: Only 'grandeur' (magnificence) can attract tourists to a fort.

questions.questionText: The minister's speech was full of ___ promises that no one believed, as they were never kept.
questions.explanation: Promises never kept are 'empty' promises.

questions.questionText: Always arriving late and missing deadlines, he showed a ___ attitude towards his job.
questions.explanation: Lateness and missed deadlines show carelessness: 'negligent'.

questions.questionText: The scientist's theory was ___ by experiments conducted by two independent labs, confirming it.
questions.explanation: 'Confirming it' signals support: 'corroborated' means confirmed.

questions.questionText: The company's profits ___ sharply during the recession, forcing it to cut jobs.
questions.explanation: Job cuts follow a steep fall, so 'plummeted' fits.

questions.questionText: Being a ___ person, he never spends a rupee without thinking twice.
questions.explanation: Thinking twice before spending describes a thrifty (frugal) person.

questions.questionText: The two neighbours finally ___ their long-standing quarrel and became friends.
questions.explanation: Becoming friends means the quarrel was settled: 'resolved'.

questions.questionText: The lawyer gave a ___ argument that left no room for doubt.
questions.explanation: An argument leaving no doubt is convincing: 'cogent'.

questions.questionText: The crowd became ___ when the match was stopped unfairly and began throwing bottles.
questions.explanation: Throwing bottles shows disorderly behaviour: 'unruly'.

questions.questionText: Her ___ in the kitchen was evident from the perfect meal she cooked.
questions.explanation: A perfect meal shows skill: 'proficiency'.

questions.questionText: The patient's condition is ___; the doctors say he may not survive the night.
questions.explanation: Possible death overnight means a grave condition: 'critical'.

questions.questionText: The old professor was known for his ___ of speech; he could say a lot in a few words.
questions.explanation: Saying much in few words is 'brevity'; 'verbosity' is the opposite.

questions.questionText: The shopkeeper's ___ reply upset the customer, who had asked politely.
questions.explanation: A rude, abrupt reply to a polite question upsets: 'curt'.

questions.questionText: A good leader must be ___ and take quick decisions in a crisis.
questions.explanation: Quick decisions require being 'decisive'.

questions.questionText: The fire was ___ before it could spread to the neighbouring houses.
questions.explanation: Stopping it from spreading means it was put out: 'extinguished'.

questions.questionText: The students were ___ by the teacher for talking during the exam.
questions.explanation: Talking during an exam draws a scolding: 'reprimanded'.

questions.questionText: The explorers faced ___ weather on the peak, with blizzards and freezing winds.
questions.explanation: Blizzards and freezing winds are harsh: 'hostile'.

questions.questionText: Though wealthy, she led a ___ life, avoiding show and luxury.
questions.explanation: 'Avoiding show and luxury' describes a modest life.

questions.questionText: The two parties could not reach a ___ and the talks collapsed.
questions.explanation: One 'reaches a compromise' in negotiations; the other nouns do not collocate with 'reach' here.

questions.questionText: The new software is ___ with all the older versions, so files open without trouble.
questions.explanation: 'Compatible with' means able to work together.

questions.questionText: The CEO's sudden ___ shocked the board, as he had held the post for only a month.
questions.explanation: Leaving a post after a month is a resignation.

questions.questionText: The soldiers showed great ___ in the face of enemy fire.
questions.explanation: Courage under fire is 'valour'.

questions.questionText: The politician's ___ remarks about the minority community sparked widespread protests.
questions.explanation: Protests follow insulting remarks: 'derogatory' means disparaging.

questions.questionText: The report was so ___ that it covered every minor detail of the project.
questions.explanation: Covering every minor detail means thorough: 'exhaustive'.

questions.questionText: Hari's ___ nature made him adjust easily to any new city he was posted to.
questions.explanation: Adjusting easily shows adaptability.

questions.questionText: The judge's verdict was ___, favouring neither side.
questions.explanation: 'Favouring neither side' = impartial; 'partial' means biased.

questions.questionText: Despite repeated warnings, he continued his ___ driving and finally met with an accident.
questions.explanation: Ignoring warnings and crashing shows reckless driving.

questions.questionText: The minister's ___ response to the question avoided giving a direct answer.
questions.explanation: Avoiding a direct answer is 'evasive'.

questions.questionText: The doctor's ___ treatment of a minor ailment was criticised as an overreaction.
questions.explanation: Overreaction implies extreme measures: 'drastic'.

questions.questionText: Her speech was so ___ that half the audience began to yawn.
questions.explanation: Yawning shows boredom caused by a dull, unvarying speech: 'monotonous'.
